metadata.name: Paul's 1st Missionary Journey
metadata.description: Paul and Barnabas travel through Cyprus and Asia Minor (~47-48 AD)

properties.name: Antioch (Syria)
properties.event_name: Sent Out by the Holy Spirit
properties.description: The Holy Spirit said, 'Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them.' They were sent off from Antioch.

properties.name: Seleucia
properties.description: Paul and Barnabas sailed from Seleucia, the port city of Antioch, beginning the first missionary journey.

properties.name: Salamis, Cyprus
properties.description: In Salamis they proclaimed the word of God in the Jewish synagogues. John Mark was with them as their helper.

properties.name: Paphos, Cyprus
properties.description: Sergius Paulus, the proconsul, summoned Paul and Barnabas. The sorcerer Elymas opposed them; Paul struck him with temporary blindness. The proconsul believed.

properties.name: Perga, Pamphylia
properties.description: At Perga, John Mark left them and returned to Jerusalem — a departure that later caused conflict between Paul and Barnabas.

properties.name: Pisidian Antioch
properties.event_name: Paul's Synagogue Sermon; Turned to Gentiles
properties.description: Paul preached in the synagogue; many Gentiles came the next Sabbath. When the Jews rejected the message, Paul declared: 'We turn to the Gentiles.'

properties.name: Iconium
properties.description: A great number of Jews and Gentiles believed. Paul and Barnabas spent considerable time, speaking boldly and performing signs and wonders.

properties.name: Lystra
properties.description: Paul healed a man lame from birth; the crowd called them gods. Then Jews from Antioch and Iconium came and stoned Paul, dragging him outside the city — but he got up.

properties.name: Derbe
properties.description: Paul and Barnabas preached the gospel in Derbe and won a large number of disciples before retracing their steps to strengthen the churches.
